An inherited directory that is gone starts the pane in home (new tab and split alike, since macOS reports a removed directory as live); a typed --cwd is still refused. creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-18: eight new tabs in 15 seconds, from Cmd+T and the Tab menu, all did nothing. The focused pane's shell was in `/Users/amterp/src/finances`, which no longer existed. A new tab starts in the focused pane's directory, so each time the daemon was asked to start a shell there, and refused:

```
daemon.pane.not_started  cwd=/Users/amterp/src/finances  error="No such file or directory (os error 2)"
core.refused  request=create_tab  reason="the daemon did not make that change: could not start /bin/zsh in /Users/amterp/src/finances: No such file or directory (os error 2) ..."
```

New tab worked again once a pane in an existing directory had focus. The window never said why (a_2jzGT81IV), so it looked like new tab was broken.

A directory nobody named shouldn't stop a tab from opening. Restoring a pane after a daemon restart already copes with this: it tries the saved directory and then home (`daemon.state.fallback` in `crates/muster-daemon/src/session.rs`). A new tab could do the same. A directory someone typed, as in `muster tab new --cwd /nope`, should probably still be refused.

The existence check has to run on the daemon's machine, because the focused pane may be on a devenv. Today the daemon cannot tell an inherited directory from a typed one: `open_a_tab` in `crates/muster-seam/src/handler.rs` fills an empty `cwd` with the focused pane's (`session::cwd_of`) before sending, so both arrive in the same field. One option is to name the pane to take the directory from instead, the way a split leaves `cwd` empty and the daemon reads the neighbour's `live_cwd`. Another is a flag telling the daemon it may fall back.

Not checked: whether a split from such a pane fails the same way. A split sends no `cwd`, and on macOS the neighbour's live directory may still read as the deleted path.
title: 🧭 A new tab is refused when the focused pane's directory no longer exists
